items.title: feat(rules): add MCP009 rule to detect hardcoded API keys and secrets in tool handlers
items.summary: Detect hardcoded credentials (e.g., `sk-...`, `ghp_...`, `AKIA...`, `Bearer ...`, or assignments to `api_key` / `secret` string literals) inside `@mcp.tool()` functions.
items.motivation: Developers prototyping MCP servers frequently paste API keys directly into tool modules before publishing. Catching high-confidence secret patterns in `mcp-doctor scan` prevents accidental credential leaks.
acceptance_criteria: Scan string constants inside decorated tool functions for common token prefixes (`ghp_`, `github_pat_`, `sk-`, `AKIA`, `xoxb-`) and sensitive variable assignments.
Register rule `MCP009` (`hardcoded-secret-in-tool`, severity `ERROR`, category `SECURITY`) via `@register_rule`.
Ignore placeholder strings such as `YOUR_API_KEY`, `example`, `<token>`, or empty strings (`os.environ[...]`).
Add unit tests covering both positive detections and placeholder/env-var non-triggers.

items.title: feat(rules): add MCP010 rule flagging outbound HTTP calls missing explicit `timeout=`
items.summary: Flag `requests.get/post/...`, `httpx.get/post/...`, and `urllib.request.urlopen(...)` calls inside MCP tools when no `timeout` keyword argument is provided.
items.motivation: An MCP tool that hangs indefinitely on a stalled upstream socket blocks the entire LLM agent turn and stdio transport pipe.
acceptance_criteria: Record outbound HTTP call AST nodes that omit `timeout=...` (or pass `timeout=None`).
Register rule `MCP010` (`missing-network-timeout`, severity `WARNING`, category `SECURITY`).
Ensure `examples/clean_server.py` continues to score `100/100 (A+)` (it already passes `timeout=5`).
Add unit tests for `requests.get(url)` (flagged) vs `requests.get(url, timeout=10)` (clean).

items.title: feat(rules): add MCP011 rule for SQL string interpolation in `.execute(...)` calls
items.summary: Detect f-strings, `%` formatting, `.format(...)`, or `+` string concatenation inside `cursor.execute(...)` / `session.execute(...)` when referencing tool parameters.
items.motivation: Database MCP servers are one of the most common MCP server types, and LLM-generated arguments can trivially trigger SQL injection if interpolated directly into SQL strings.
acceptance_criteria: Detect `.execute(...)` / `.executemany(...)` calls whose first argument is an `ast.JoinedStr` (f-string), `ast.BinOp` (`%` or `+`), or `.format()` call referencing a tool parameter.
Register `MCP011` (`sql-string-interpolation`, severity `ERROR`, category `SECURITY`).
Allow parameterized queries (`cursor.execute('SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = ?', (user_id,))`) without false positives.
Add unit tests for f-string SQL vs parameterized SQL.

items.title: feat(reporters): add `--format github` reporter for inline GitHub Actions PR annotations
items.summary: Add a `--format github` output option to `mcp-doctor scan` that emits GitHub Actions workflow commands (`::error`, `::warning`, `::notice`).
items.motivation: Emitting `::error file=server.py,line=24,title=MCP005 (dangerous-shell-execution)::...` lets GitHub render inline annotations directly on changed lines in Pull Request diffs without requiring GitHub Advanced Security / SARIF upload.
acceptance_criteria: Implement `render_github_annotations(report: ScanReport) -> str` mapping `ERROR -> ::error`, `WARNING -> ::warning`, `INFO -> ::notice`.
Properly escape `%`, `\r`, and `\n` in workflow command messages per GitHub Actions spec.
Wire `--format github` into `mcp-doctor scan` CLI choices.
Add CLI tests verifying exact annotation lines.

items.title: feat(rules): add MCP012 rule when tool parameters have no description
items.summary: Emit an `INFO`-level diagnostic (`MCP012`, `undocumented-parameter`) when a tool parameter lacks a docstring `Args:` entry or JSON Schema `description`.
items.motivation: Even when a tool has a top-level description, undocumented parameters (like `mode: str` or `flags: int`) force agents to guess valid values and semantics.
acceptance_criteria: Support extracting parameter descriptions from `Annotated[T, Field(description='...')]` in `python_ast.py` in addition to `Args:` / `:param:` docstrings.
Register `MCP012` (`undocumented-parameter`, severity `INFO`, category `SCHEMA`).
Verify `examples/clean_server.py` and `examples/tools_manifest.json` remain warning/info-clean.
Add unit tests for documented vs undocumented parameters in both Python and JSON manifests.

items.title: feat(parsers): add TypeScript MCP SDK (`server.tool(...)`) static loader
items.summary: Support scanning `.ts` and `.js` MCP servers built with `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` (`server.tool(name, description, zodSchema, handler)` and `registerTool(...)`).
items.motivation: Roughly half of public MCP servers are written in TypeScript. Supporting `.ts`/`.js` files without requiring a Node runtime makes `mcp-doctor` a universal cross-language MCP auditor.
acceptance_criteria: Extract tool name, description, basic Zod parameter names/types (`z.string()`, `z.number().max(...)`, `z.any()`), and dangerous sinks (`child_process.exec`, `eval`) from `.ts`/`.js` files.
Register `.ts` and `.js` extensions in `discover_candidate_files` and `scan_paths`.
Ignore `*.d.ts` declaration files and `node_modules`.
Add fixture-based tests covering clean and vulnerable TypeScript MCP servers.

items.title: feat(cli): add `mcp-doctor init` command to scaffold `.mcp-doctor.toml` and CI workflow
items.summary: Add an `mcp-doctor init [--github-action]` subcommand that generates a commented `.mcp-doctor.toml` config file and optional `.github/workflows/mcp-doctor.yml`.
items.motivation: One-command onboarding drastically lowers friction for maintainers adopting `mcp-doctor` in existing MCP server repositories.
acceptance_criteria: Create `.mcp-doctor.toml` with documented defaults (`max-tool-tokens`, `max-server-tokens`, `ignore`, `exclude`).
Refuse to overwrite existing files unless `--force` is passed.
When `--github-action` is passed, write `.github/workflows/mcp-doctor.yml` referencing `RANJITHROSAN17/mcp-doctor@main`.
Add unit tests covering fresh creation, existing-file protection, and `--force`.

items.title: feat(rules): add MCP013 rule for unsafe deserialization (`pickle.loads`, `yaml.load`)
items.summary: Detect `pickle.loads`, `pickle.load`, `marshal.loads`, `shelve.open`, and `yaml.load` (without `SafeLoader`) inside MCP tool functions.
items.motivation: Deserializing untrusted payloads inside an MCP tool leads directly to arbitrary code execution.
acceptance_criteria: Detect unsafe deserialization calls in `python_ast.py`, treating `yaml.safe_load(...)` and `yaml.load(..., Loader=yaml.SafeLoader)` as safe.
Register `MCP013` (`unsafe-deserialization`, severity `ERROR`, category `SECURITY`).
Add unit tests verifying `yaml.load(data)` triggers `MCP013` while `yaml.safe_load(data)` passes.

items.title: feat(parsers): expand Pydantic `BaseModel` and `TypedDict` parameter schemas in Python AST loader
items.summary: Resolve in-file `BaseModel` and `TypedDict` classes referenced by `@mcp.tool()` parameters so nested fields are audited for types, bounds, and token footprint.
items.motivation: Many FastMCP servers group tool arguments into a Pydantic `BaseModel` (`def search(req: SearchRequest)`). Expanding its fields unlocks accurate `MCP002`/`MCP003`/`MCP004` diagnostics.
acceptance_criteria: Index class definitions inheriting from `BaseModel` or `TypedDict` in the same module.
Expand their annotated attributes (including `Field(le=..., max_length=..., description=...)`) into `ParameterSpec` entries.
Update token estimation accordingly and add unit tests.

items.title: feat(cli): add `mcp-doctor inspect --stdio <cmd>` live MCP server introspection
items.summary: Spawn any MCP server command over JSON-RPC 2.0 stdio, perform handshake + `tools/list`, and run all schema/contract/token rules on the live advertised tools.
items.motivation: Dynamic MCP servers (written in Go, Rust, Java, or dynamically registered in Python) can be audited at runtime via standard MCP `tools/list` JSON-RPC without needing language-specific AST parsers.
acceptance_criteria: Implement minimal stdlib `subprocess` JSON-RPC 2.0 `initialize` -> `notifications/initialized` -> `tools/list` client with configurable timeout.
Feed returned `tools` array through existing `json_manifest` normalizer and scan engine.
Test against a tiny mock stdio Python script in `tests/`.

items.title: feat(reporters): add standalone interactive HTML report (`--format html`)
items.summary: Generate a zero-external-asset HTML dashboard (`--format html`) displaying the health grade, per-tool token usage bars, and filterable diagnostics.
items.motivation: Teams running `mcp-doctor` in CI artifacts want a single shareable HTML report with zero CDN dependencies.
acceptance_criteria: Emit valid self-contained HTML5 with inline CSS and escaped diagnostic strings (`html.escape`).
Include health score badge, per-tool token breakdown table, and severity filter toggles.
Add unit tests verifying HTML escaping and CLI `--format html` execution.

items.title: feat(cli): add `--baseline <path>` support to suppress pre-existing findings during incremental adoption
items.summary: Allow generating and passing a baseline JSON snapshot so CI only fails on newly introduced findings.
items.motivation: Large existing MCP servers (50+ tools) need a way to turn on `mcp-doctor` in CI immediately without fixing every historical warning on day one.
acceptance_criteria: Support `--write-baseline .mcp-doctor-baseline.json` and `--baseline .mcp-doctor-baseline.json`.
Match baseline entries by `(rule_id, tool_name, source_file)` fingerprint rather than brittle line numbers.
Add CLI tests demonstrating existing findings suppressed while new findings fail.

items.title: feat(rules): add server-wide token budget warning (`MCP014`) when total context tax exceeds `max-server-tokens`
items.summary: Emit `MCP014` (`excessive-server-tokens`) when the sum of all discovered tools' estimated tokens exceeds `ScanConfig.max_server_tokens` (default `4000`).
items.motivation: Even if each individual tool stays at 200 tokens, exposing 35 tools on a single MCP server silently burns 7,000+ tokens on every conversation turn.
acceptance_criteria: Register `MCP014` (`excessive-server-tokens`, severity `WARNING`, category `TOKENS`).
Trigger once when `sum(t.estimated_tokens for t in tools) > config.max_server_tokens`, naming the top 3 heaviest tools in the message.
Add unit tests with custom `ScanConfig(max_server_tokens=...)`.

items.title: feat(parsers): support YAML MCP / OpenAI tool manifests (`*.yaml`, `*.yml`)
items.summary: Load tool definitions from YAML manifests when `PyYAML` is installed (gracefully skipping when absent).
items.motivation: Agent frameworks (CrewAI, AutoGen, declarative MCP gateways) frequently store tool schemas in `.yaml` files.
acceptance_criteria: Use `yaml.safe_load` when `pyyaml` is available; never use unsafe `yaml.load`.
Reuse `_normalize_tool_entry` from `json_manifest.py` to avoid code duplication.
Add unit tests for YAML tool manifests and non-tool YAML configs (e.g., GitHub Actions workflows must be ignored cleanly).

items.title: feat(parsers): intra-module helper function taint propagation for security rules (MCP005-MCP007)
items.summary: Follow 1-hop calls from `@mcp.tool()` functions to module-local helper functions (`_run_cmd(...)`, `_fetch(...)`) when extracting `CodeSink` entries.
items.motivation: Production MCP servers often delegate execution to private helper functions in the same file. Propagating tainted parameter flow across 1-hop helper calls significantly increases security recall.
acceptance_criteria: Index top-level helper functions in the same AST module and detect sinks reachable when a tool passes a parameter into a helper call.
Avoid infinite recursion on mutually recursive helpers.
Add unit tests verifying sinks inside `_helper(url)` are attributed to the calling `@mcp.tool()`.

items.title: feat(rules): add MCP009 protocol / transport validation
items.summary: Validate MCP protocol and transport configuration with actionable diagnostics.
items.motivation: Transport and protocol mismatches should be visible before deployment.
acceptance_criteria: Use a non-conflicting rule ID and document supported protocol assumptions.
Test supported and unsupported transport configurations without executing a server.

items.title: feat(engine): add runtime risk scoring (severity + exploitability + mitigation)
items.summary: Add configurable risk scoring using finding severity, exploitability and available mitigations.
items.motivation: A documented score can help operators prioritize findings consistently.
acceptance_criteria: Define and document deterministic scoring weights and output fields.
Test score boundaries, mitigated findings and compatibility with existing reports.

items.title: feat(engine): baseline comparison --current vs --previous scan
items.summary: Compare current and previous scan results to identify new, resolved and unchanged findings.
items.motivation: Scan comparisons make regressions and remediation progress visible.
acceptance_criteria: Specify stable diagnostic matching keys and an explicit comparison interface.
Test added, resolved and unchanged findings, including malformed baseline input.

items.title: feat(cli): add mcp-doctor simulate --model cost benchmark
items.summary: Integrate model-specific token-cost estimates into the mcp-doctor simulate command.
items.motivation: Operators need transparent estimates of tool-schema context costs.
acceptance_criteria: Load tool schemas from the requested input rather than a placeholder example.
Document pricing units and assumptions; test model selection and unknown-model behavior.

items.title: feat(policies): strict-prod + enterprise-gov policy templates
items.summary: Provide documented strict-production and enterprise-governance policy presets.
items.motivation: Reusable policy settings reduce inconsistent deployment checks.
acceptance_criteria: Define supported preset settings and explicit override precedence.
Test preset loading, invalid names and backward compatibility with existing configuration.

items.title: feat(dashboard): live audit-report.json feed + trend analytics
items.summary: Expose audit-report JSON data and historical trends in the dashboard.
items.motivation: Teams need a readable view of audit results and changes over time.
acceptance_criteria: Specify a versioned report feed and history format.
Test missing reports, escaped untrusted display content and trend calculations.

items.title: feat(plugin): rule-pack marketplace (custom + community rules)
items.summary: Design explicit opt-in discovery and configuration of third-party rule packs.
items.motivation: Organizations need extensible checks without implicitly trusting or running arbitrary plugins.
acceptance_criteria: Document the plugin trust boundary and require explicit opt-in.
Reject duplicate rule IDs and test disabled plugins and load errors.
